record.original_question: An isometric action of a group G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for every ε > 0 there exist R, N > 0 such that for every two points x, y with d(x, y) ⩾ R, there are at most N elements g ∈ G satisfying d(x, gx) ⩽ ε and d(y, gy) ⩽ ε. A group is said to be acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical action on a hyperbolic space with unbounded orbits. Is the automorphism group of a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group also acylindrically hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. An isometric action of a group $G$ on a metric space $(S,d)$ is called acylindrical if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exist constants $R, N > 0$ such that for any two points $x, y \in S$ with $d(x,y) \geq R$, the number of elements $g \in G$ satisfying both $d(x, gx) \leq \varepsilon$ and $d(y, gy) \leq \varepsilon$ is at most $N$. A group $G$ is called acylindrically hyperbolic if $G$ is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical isometric action on some Gromov-hyperbolic geodesic metric space with unbounded orbits.

Question. Let $G$ be a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group. Is the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ also acylindrically hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is known to be answered affirmatively in several important sub-cases: Genevois (2020/2021) proved that the automorphism group of every infinitely-ended finitely generated group is acylindrically hyperbolic, covering Aut(F_n) for n≥2; the automorphism group of any one-ended hyperbolic group is acylindrically hyperbolic (Genevois–Horbez); and the result is known for groups hyperbolic relative to proper finitely generated subgroups. A general answer for all finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic groups does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Acylindrical hyperbolicity of automorphism groups of infinitely-ended groups
status_evidence.snippet: The automorphism group of every infinitely-ended finitely generated group is acylindrically hyperbolic; in particular Aut(F_n) is acylindrically hyperbolic for every n≥2.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results for infinitely-ended finitely generated groups.

status_evidence.title: Negative curvature in automorphism groups of one-ended hyperbolic groups
status_evidence.snippet: The automorphism group of any one-ended hyperbolic group is acylindrically hyperbolic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive result for one-ended hyperbolic groups.

status_evidence.title: Acylindrically hyperbolic group - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Survey article describing classes known to be acylindrically hyperbolic.
status_evidence.claim: No general theorem stated for Aut(G) when G is acylindrically hyperbolic.
